scope: Analytic cone/torus surface-surface intersection in the coaxial configuration (eleventh analytic SS slice, one cell): native intersect_cone_torus in crates/brep-core/src/intersections/cone_torus.rs, bridge op brep_intersect_cone_torus, typed TS adapter intersectConeTorus. The cell reuses both existing recognizers unchanged (plane_cone::recognize_cone for the exact canonical conical frustum solid — four rational ruled side patches linearly interpolated between the two radius rings, a bilinear cap per nonzero ring, a true apex admitted when exactly one radius is zero, an equal-radius frustum refused as a cylinder; plane_torus::recognize_torus for the exact sixteen-patch strict ring-torus solid with tensor-product weights [[1,w,1],[w,w^2,w],[1,w,1]], w = cos(pi/4), R - r >= 1e-5; rigid affine placements admitted). The cone operand is always first — swapped order is an explicit unsupported_surface region. Coaxiality is certified, never forced: a pure-rounding axis tilt (64 binary64 epsilons plus the recognition-error angular allowances) or center-line offset (64 epsilons of the axial/radius terms plus both recognition deviations) snaps to coaxial, a recognition-scale tilt or offset (1e-9) reports near_coincidence, and a clearly tilted or off-axis pair is unsupported_surface (the general cone/torus pair is a quartic, out of scope — no numerical fallback). Either axis orientation is admitted: the anti-axial pair is oriented by the sign of the axes' dot product (as in cone_cone); the meridian circle is symmetric in z, so the sign enters only the height map and the torus profile angles. Both surfaces are surfaces of revolution about the shared axis, so the section reduces to line/circle in the meridian half-plane (rho >= 0, z): the cone side is the slanted line (rho, z) = (r_b + m t, z_b + s t) in the cone's own axial parameter t against the torus meridian circle (rho - R)^2 + z^2 = r^2 — one exact quadratic (1+m^2) t^2 + 2 B t + C = 0 whose discriminant is r^2 (1+m^2) - D^2 with D = (R - r_b) s + z_b m the signed line/circle-center cross (the line passes the meridian circle center at distance |D|/sqrt(1+m^2)). Classification uses outward binary64 bands widened by both recognition deviations: a provable miss (distance > r + band) resolves empty by the interval signs; a tangent line (distance == r within the band, a double root) whose foot lands on the finite side segment stays tangency_or_multiple_root, never a guessed circle (a tangency foot provably beyond the finite height belongs to the rim bands); distinct roots revolve into exact circles (radius rho* = r_b + m t*, height z* = z_b + s t*) clipped by the cone's finite height — a root provably beyond a ring plane is honestly absent, a root within the band of a ring plane is the rim contact (unresolved). Rim bands ((r_ring - R)^2 + h_q^2 == r^2 within the band, also owning the zero-radius apex ring) stay tangency_or_multiple_root independent of the side classification. Cap-plane contacts: a ring plane at torus-axial height h_c with |h_c| < r provable cuts the exact circle pair R +- sqrt(r^2 - h_c^2) (the plane/torus perpendicular branch reduced to the ring disk): a circle provably inside the ring disk is a cap circle component, a radius equal to the ring radius within the band is the rim tangency (unresolved), a radius provably beyond is absent, and |h_c| == r within the band is the plane/tube tangency (unresolved). Resolved contacts are exact rational circles (degree 2, knots 0..=4, four 90-degree arcs, weights cos(pi/4)) with UV lifts on both surfaces: the iso-v line at the exact height fraction on all four cone side patches, the exact four-arc UV circle of radius rho/(2 r_ring) about [1/2, 1/2] on a ring cap, and the torus iso-v parallels at the exact profile angle phi = atan2(z, rho - R) through the exact rational 90-degree-arc parameter map t = s/(1+s), s = sqrt(2) tan(phi/2)/(1 - tan(phi/2)), one degree-1 line per revolution quadrant patch of the profile row. permitsTopologyChange stays false; nothing here is consumed by the Boolean pipeline.
